item.title: EU top court new search tool dubbed a ‘disaster’ by lawyers
item.description: What was announced as a ‘new gateway to European justice’ has law scholars and professionals up in arms about their ability to conduct research effectively, and potentially “de-democratising access to public data, fuelling an industry of commercial actors”.

item.title: Gay Pride organiser faces jail as Hungary tightens grip on civil rights
item.description: It is the first known case in the EU where a human-rights defender faces imprisonment for organising a Pride march, according to civil society.

item.title: Spain seeks probe into AI-generated child sexual abuse on TikTok, X and Meta
item.description: Spain’s government has asked its public prosecutor on Tuesday to investigate TikTok, X, and Meta for potentially spreading AI-generated child sexual abuse material on their platforms.

item.title: Listen: Could EU migration policy lead to ICE-style raids?
item.description: The EU is readying new rules to speed up deportations of irregular migrants — but dozens of NGOs warn the measures could mirror hard-line tactics used by US immigration authorities. Is Europe about to take a tougher turn on migration?

item.title: Leaked details of what will be in Brussels’ new ‘Made in Europe’ rules
item.description: The European Commission is planning to introduce “Made in EU” requirements across a wide range of strategic sectors, from chips, cars, and chemicals to quantum technologies and renewable energy.

item.title: A fast-tracked Ukraine EU accession by 2027? Here are three dilemmas
item.description: The idea of a fast-tracked Ukraine accession to the EU, as early as 2027, is gaining ground in Brussels. But urgency must not come at the expense of principle. The greater risk today is not moving too fast but moving halfway, warns the European Policy Centre.

item.title: Listen: Orbán on the brink in Hungary elections – what’s at stake for the EU?
item.description: In Hungary, prime minister Viktor Orbán could lose the next elections after 10 years in power. But what would this mean for the EU? Could the traditional Hungarian veto become a thing of the past?

item.title: Nuclear weapons talk to fresh arms deals: how Poland’s defence surge is reshaping Europe’s frontline
item.description: Poland considers developing its own nuclear capabilities amid rising Russian threats, while the EU approves €43.7bn from the SAFE programme for defence modernisation. Meanwhile, allies including Germany and France show growing interest in Polish weapons such as the Piorun system.

item.title: Former diplomats accuse French foreign minister of disinformation over UN envoy Albanese
item.description: The ex-ministers, ambassadors, and diplomats accuse French foreign minister Jean-Noël Barrot of spreading disinformation and called for a correction of his comments about UNrapporteur for Palestine, Francesca Albanese.

item.title: ‘Frog toxin’ that killed Navalny was likely lab-made, says expert
item.description: The 'frog' poison that killed Navalny was hard to hide and likely made in a high-end lab, according to a Belgian toxicologist.
